builds.name: Reference: Ranked jungle core
builds.goal: Reference for Quinn: the core and runes ranked Emerald+ jungle players use most (3,050 ranked Emerald+ games with this core on OP.GG, patch 16.20, 54.8% win rate).
builds.hypothesis: A roaming ranged duelist who consumes Harrier marks for movement and attack speed, using Vault to manage distance. The current jungle provider core anchors this plan; later slots are observed options or reviewed kit completions. Core in purchase order: Hubris → The Collector → Lord Dominik's Regards. Electrocute keystone as played in those games. Remaining slots: Boots of Swiftness, Infinity Edge, Guardian Angel.
builds.summary: The proven jungle baseline: Hubris → The Collector → Lord Dominik's Regards, with Electrocute.
testPlan: Play it in jungle as your control build. Follow the purchase order; the core (Hubris → The Collector → Lord Dominik's Regards) is what ranked players complete first.
Record kills, deaths, damage dealt and the minute you finish each core item, then compare other builds against these numbers in similar games.
Adapt the last two items to the enemy team: armor or magic resist against fed carries, anti-heal against healing, penetration once enemies stack resists.
failureConditions: Your results with this build fall clearly below the 54.8% ranked baseline over several games in the same role.
The enemy team composition makes the core items poor answers; swap the flexible slots before abandoning the core.
tradeoffs: Proven and predictable, so opponents know what to expect. It is a starting point, not the best build for every matchup.
The observed core and individual options do not establish six-item build statistics. Late slots are kit-based inferences.
Six-slot completion is our kit-based inference, not an observed six-item win-rate build.  Situational options replace an appropriate slot; they are not added as a seventh item.
buyOrder: Core in purchase order: Hubris → The Collector → Lord Dominik's Regards.
Boots after the first item unless the lane needs them earlier.
coverageNotes: Source: OP.GG ranked Emerald+ solo/duo, patch 16.20, checked 2026-10-14. Core items and rune page are observed; later slots are observed options or reviewed completions. Win rates describe those games, not a prediction for yours.
builds.author: Rift Build Lab ranked data

kitEvidence.formula:
Passive: Attacking a Harrier target grants Quinn [(0.28 / 0.41 / 0.54 / 0.67 / 0.8) × 100]% Attack Speed and [(0.2 / 0.25 / 0.3 / 0.35 / 0.4) × 100]% Move Speed for [2] seconds.

Active: Valor reveals a large area nearby for [2] seconds.

Quinn calls to Valor, pairing up after channeling for 2 seconds gaining [(0.7 / 1 / 1.3) × 100]% Move Speed and allowing her to Recast this Ability. Attacking or using {{Spell_QuinnQ_Name}} or {{Spell_QuinnE_Name}} automatically Recasts this Ability.

Recast: Quinn and Valor perform an aerial maneuver, dealing [60 / 90 / 120 + (0.35) × AD[statFormula=2]] physical damage, marking champions with Harrier, and ending this Ability.

Every @f1@ seconds, Valor marks a nearby enemy with Harrier, revealing it for [4] seconds and causing Quinn's next Attack %i:OnHit% On-Hit against them to deal [(characterLevelInterpolation(15 → 120; raw flags preserved) + (0.4) × AD[statFormula=2]) × (1)] bonus physical damage.

Quinn dashes to an enemy, dealing [40 / 65 / 90 / 115 / 140 + (0.2) × AD[statFormula=2]] physical damage and marking them with Harrier. Quinn then leaps backwards from the target, slightly Knocking them Back and Slowing them by [50]%, decaying over [1.5] seconds.

Quinn orders Valor to dive, making the first enemy hit with Harrier, reducing their vision radius for [1.75] seconds and dealing [65 / 100 / 135 / 170 / 205 + (0.8 / 0.85 / 0.9 / 0.95 / 1) × AD[statFormula=2] + (0.5) × AP] physical damage to all surrounding enemies.

If the first enemy struck is not a champion, it is Disarmed for [1.75] seconds.

builds.name: Mark reset Spellblade
builds.summary: Use separated Q/E marks for timed spell-followed attacks.
builds.goal: Use separated Q/E marks for timed spell-followed attacks.
builds.hypothesis: Q and E each mark Harrier, whose consumption grants W attack speed and movement. Trinity and Stormrazor reward actual attacks after approach spells; Cleaver supports physical packets. E recoil creates a new spacing decision instead of requiring continuous melee contact.
testPlan: Required state: Consume one mark before applying the next and wait for Spellblade readiness.
Compare Q-attack-E-attack against Q-E-attack, logging Harrier and Spellblade separately.

Run three trials at matched level, ranks, gold and target defenses. Repeat against a moving opponent with a fixed incoming damage pattern. Record damage packets, missed actions, resource cost and survival separately.
Keep souls, health/mana, form, item/rune stacks, transformations and game time finite and explicitly recorded. No free full ramp or infinite scaling.
failureConditions: Overwriting marks or E recoil moving out of range loses the intended attacks.
The narrow damage gain does not repay lost access, survival, wave control or allied utility.
tradeoffs: Rejected assumption: Applying two marks before attacking does not bank two Harrier consumptions.
Confidence: plausible. Source-compatible reasoning is not in-game validation or proof of novelty/optimality.
buyOrder: Candidate six slots: Trinity Force, Stormrazor, Black Cleaver, Bloodthirster, Edge of Night, Berserker's Greaves. Compare two-item checkpoints before the final six-slot test; this list is not a lane shopping order.
Keep role-appropriate starters, boots and support quest/vision obligations. If the full candidate assumes farmed income, compare it separately from support income.
coverageNotes: Only Cassiopeia Q/E and Sett W have numerical adapters. Even there, these other objectives and item/rune interactions may fall outside the model.
Proc inheritance, crit, pet hits and conditional helpers remain uncertain until observed. No completed mathematical maximum is claimed.

builds.name: Situational adaptation: Physical matchup
builds.goal: Situational adaptation for Quinn: adapt to the specified fight rather than assume one universal build
builds.hypothesis: A roaming ranged duelist who consumes Harrier marks for movement and attack speed, using Vault to manage distance. Record Harrier mark consumption, Vault spacing and real roaming time. Burst/lethality may win a pick while failing against durable targets or losing carry DPS. Armor and access may turn survival into additional attack/spell windows.
builds.summary: Armor and access may turn survival into additional attack/spell windows.
testPlan: Kit question for Quinn: Record Harrier mark consumption, Vault spacing and real roaming time. Burst/lethality may win a pick while failing against durable targets or losing carry DPS.

Start with the early core (Stridebreaker, then matchup armor) plus appropriate boots at matched gold. Record level, actual ability ranks, forms, resource and item transformations; six-item results do not establish lane strength. Use your intended lane or jungle role; jungle starters and early consumables are outside the final six slots.

Compare against the reference route at the same level, gold spent, finite stacks and opponent setup. Record unused gold; isolate an item change before changing runes. Run three repeatable trials of a short trade and a ten-second fight. Record damage actually landed, attacks/casts, misses, remaining resource and survival. Record available/max mana and any transformed mana-item state.

Measure the actual interaction before granting item/rune procs: Armor and access may turn survival into additional attack/spell windows. Test once stationary, then with a moving opponent and a fixed incoming damage pattern. Choose the opponent profile this defensive route is intended to address, then repeat against the wrong damage type.

Q evidence: Quinn calls Valor to mark an enemy and hinder its vision before damaging all enemies in the immediate area. Keep finite champion/item/rune stacks explicit. Use Practice Tool, a custom match or your own replay; no numerical adapter is available for this champion.
failureConditions: Randuin is conditional on the enemy attack/crit profile; it costs an offensive slot.

The route fails Quinn's stated kit question: Record Harrier mark consumption, Vault spacing and real roaming time. Burst/lethality may win a pick while failing against durable targets or losing carry DPS.
Higher dummy damage is offset by fewer landed actions, deaths before the useful window, or worse ally utility.
tradeoffs: Randuin is conditional on the enemy attack/crit profile; it costs an offensive slot.
Full cost 16,100 gold; delayed items, resource starvation and the two-item spike must be judged separately.
Counter-items are conditional. Change boots/defense for the real matchup, then record the modified setup.
buyOrder: Stridebreaker, then matchup armor. Adapt component timing to lane/jungle pressure; do not blindly follow the displayed six-item order.
Keep appropriate boots while building the early core; swap boots only when the measured matchup justifies it.
Randuin's Omen, Spirit Visage, Sterak's Gage are later or conditional slots; do not postpone necessary protection for a six-item ceiling.
Record available/max mana and any transformed mana-item state.
coverageNotes: No numerical damage or survival adapter exists for this champion. Loading this proposal opens a manual test sheet, not calculated damage.
Source formulas remain in Champion kit. Symbolic values, unresolved tokens and helper records are evidence to inspect, not a certified executable simulator.
Legal source item/rune references were checked; retained map flags cannot prove every live-shop condition. Confirm shop eligibility, exact on-hit/on-attack rules and real proc cooldowns in game.

builds.name: Valor critical open
builds.summary: Test whether returning from Valor can start Fiendhunter's attack window.
builds.goal: Test whether returning from Valor can start Fiendhunter's attack window.
builds.hypothesis: R's return maneuver marks champions; Fiendhunter grants enhanced basic attacks after ultimate casting and RFC offers one safer opening attack. W then grants speed after mark consumption. Infinity Edge and Collector emphasize the finite critical opening rather than Q spell crit.
testPlan: Required state: Recorded R cast/recast time, energized RFC ready and accessible marked target.
Mount for two, eight and fifteen seconds; log Fiendhunter availability on dismount and first three attacks.

Run three trials at matched level, ranks, gold and target defenses. Repeat against a moving opponent with a fixed incoming damage pattern. Record damage packets, missed actions, resource cost and survival separately.
Keep souls, health/mana, form, item/rune stacks, transformations and game time finite and explicitly recorded. No free full ramp or infinite scaling.
failureConditions: Travel consumes the item window or the dismount does not retrigger it.
The narrow damage gain does not repay lost access, survival, wave control or allied utility.
tradeoffs: Rejected assumption: R's automatic recast is not established as a fresh item ultimate trigger.
Confidence: speculative. Source-compatible reasoning is not in-game validation or proof of novelty/optimality.
